account: Researchers at the Technical University of Munich placed an acoustic recorder on the roof of a housing complex in Munich, Germany, and between June and October 2021 recorded one minute in every ten around sunrise over 60 days, for 15.5 hours of audio. Two experts identified every bird call. The team ran BirdNET, a deep-learning bird sound recognizer from the Cornell Lab of Ornithology and Chemnitz University of Technology, with 24 combinations of settings at four time scales. Performance varied widely (F1 scores of 0.46 to 0.84). With tuned settings and data pooled over longer periods, BirdNET came close to the experts (F1 0.84). It missed five of the 23 species that the experts found and found one species that the experts had missed. PLOS One published the study on 11 September 2025. The authors recorded at one urban site, and they recommend basic validation of BirdNET output.

ai_role.statement: BirdNET and the experts worked on the same recordings, so the authors measure the agreement of the tool with expert identification directly.
